tests: routing — one cause spanning two modules yields one entry in the owner, not a copy in each
setup: None. The finding below is a fixture: it is deliberately adjacent to the documented vendor/shared drift without being it, so the correct outcome is a write rather than a dedup drop.
query: Розібрався нарешті. Клієнт і сервер розійшлись не в самих типах, а в тому, що client/vitest.config.ts мапить @devdigest/shared на локальну копію в client/src/vendor/shared, а серверний tsconfig — на server/src/vendor/shared. Тобто тест на клієнті зелений проти застарілої копії й ніколи не побачить розходження. Причина на боці клієнта. Заверши сесію.
expected_behavior: Writes ONE entry, not two — no copy of the same insight in both client/INSIGHTS.md and server/INSIGHTS.md
Routes it to client/INSIGHTS.md, since the query states the cause lives on the client side
Names both paths in the same bullet's evidence — client/vitest.config.ts and server/src/vendor/shared (or the server tsconfig)
Does not silently sync or edit either vendor/shared directory — both are coordination-only per root CLAUDE.md
If it judges this a duplicate of the documented vendor/shared drift, it says so and names where — that is an acceptable outcome, but it must be argued, not skipped in silence
Does not edit any CLAUDE.md; if it thinks a rule is warranted, it proposes one and waits
verify_after: git status --short — exactly one INSIGHTS.md modified; no CLAUDE.md and no vendor/shared path touched
why_this_matters: The routing rule that replaced 'write the part relevant to each, to each file'. Two copies of one insight drift apart, and a journal that contradicts itself is worse than an empty one. Also checks that a cross-module finding does not tempt the agent into the do-not-touch vendored directories.
